svg.aria-label: How to write 准: 10 strokes · 9 pen lifts · 10 movements
svg.title: Writing 准
svg.desc: 10 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of 准 (chinese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansSC-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after Hanzi Writer Data 准.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–10 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/%E5%87%86.json>. Source note on variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies ten ordered strokes for 准, in two pieces. Medians 1–2 draw the ice piece as 冷 opens: a dot, then a stroke rising to the right. Medians 3–10 draw the right side: a left-falling stroke, a long vertical down the left, a dot at the top right, three short horizontals, a vertical down through them, then a long horizontal at the foot. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians use the same coordinate system for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. This learner path adapts those ten ordered medians to the vendored Noto Sans SC outline while preserving their order, their directions and nine intervening pen lifts; stroke widths and proportions differ between the Arphic-derived source graphics and Noto Sans SC.
